 Gaming GameNative just fixed PC gaming on Pixels and Exynos-powered Galaxy phones
 No Snapdragon? No problem, as the latest update brings major fixes. Hadlee Simons • Nov 19, 2026 — 3:56 AM ET 
 • • Hadlee Simons / Android Authority Add Android Authority on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover TL;DR 
 The GameNative v1.4.1 release preview is now available and brings much better support for non-Snapdragon devices.
 The update specifically fixes major graphical problems on devices like the Pixel 6 to Pixel 10, as well as Exynos-powered Galaxy phones.
 This GameNative release also brings an Optimize feature that tunes your game based on preset goals.
 GameNative is still one of the best ways to locally run PC games on your Android device. The app works best on Snapdragon-powered devices, although the team previously introduced support for other chipmakers a while back. Now, the latest update brings great news if you’ve got a Pixel or Exynos-powered device.
 GameNative v1.4.1 has been released on GitHub as a preview, and it brings updated support for devices with Mali, PowerVR, and Xclipse graphics. The team specifically updated the “wrapper-gamenative” graphics driver. Check out the table below for a better idea of what’s been fixed.
 Discord/GameNative This update is particularly welcomed for the Pixel 10 series , which previously crashed when rendering via DXVK, VKD3D, and OpenGL. It’s unclear whether this new version of GameNative fixes any major graphical problems on the Pixel 11 series , which also uses a PowerVR GPU. Nevertheless, the table shows that you can also expect significant improvements for the Pixel 6 and Pixel 7 phones.
 Samsung owners will also be glad to see that the Exynos-powered Galaxy S24, Galaxy S26 , and several other Exynos-toting models have also received fixes. Meanwhile, the MediaTek-toting Galaxy Tab S10 Plus and Galaxy Tab S11 also receive fixes for major graphical issues. I wouldn’t expect my favorite games to start working on Pixels and Exynos-powered Galaxy phones as a result of this update, but it should certainly bring a major compatibility and performance upgrade.
 There’s more to GameNative v1.4.1 than fixes for non-Snapdragon platforms, though. The app now offers an Optimize feature which can effectively tune a game for you based on several preset goals. These presets are Balanced, Quality, Performance, Power and heat, Potato, and Off. Users can try this feature on three games, although it’s otherwise tied to the app’s $5/month membership plan.
 Other notable changes this time include Ubisoft Connect support in Steam games, themes, shared shader and FEX caching, full controller-based navigation, and local cloud save backups.
